title: Cost of binary search
statement: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
explanation: Each comparison discards half of the remaining range, so after k steps n / 2^k elements remain. The search ends when that reaches 1, which takes about log2(n) steps.

title: Array or linked list?
statement: Which operation is typically O(1) for an array but O(n) for a singly linked list?
options: Read the element at index i
explanation: An array computes the memory address of element i directly from the start address and i. A linked list has to follow i pointers. Inserting or deleting at the head is O(1) for the linked list.

title: Stack behaviour
statement: You push 1, 2, 3 onto an empty stack, then pop once. Which value comes out?
explanation: A stack is last-in first-out, so the most recently pushed value (3) is removed first.

title: Queue behaviour
statement: You enqueue A, B, C into an empty queue and then dequeue once. What comes out?
explanation: A queue is first-in first-out, so the element that has waited longest (A) leaves first.

title: Hash tables
statement: Two different keys produce the same hash index in a hash table. Which statements are true? (choose all that apply)
options: It is called overflow and the program must crash
The table can chain entries in a list at that index
The table can probe for another free slot
The second key is always discarded
explanation: A collision is expected, because there are far more possible keys than slots. Separate chaining stores several entries per slot; open addressing probes for another slot. Neither discards data, so the other statements are false.

title: What stops recursion?
statement: A recursive function never reaches its base case. What is the most likely result?
options: The call stack grows until a stack overflow error
explanation: Every call adds a frame to the call stack. Without a base case the calls never return, so the stack eventually runs out of space.

title: Stable sorting
statement: What does it mean for a sorting algorithm to be stable?
options: Equal elements keep their original relative order
It always runs in O(n log n)
explanation: If two records compare equal, a stable sort leaves them in the order they started. This matters when sorting by one column after another, for example by surname after sorting by first name.

title: Encapsulation
statement: Which choice best describes encapsulation?
options: Making every field public for easy access
Bundling data with the methods that use it and hiding internal details
explanation: Encapsulation keeps an object's state behind a controlled interface, so the object can protect its own rules (for example "a balance never goes negative") and its internals can change without breaking callers.

title: Polymorphism
statement: A variable of type Shape holds a Circle object. Calling area() runs the Circle version. What is this called?
explanation: The method that runs is chosen from the actual runtime type of the object, not from the declared type of the variable. Overloading, by contrast, chooses between methods with different parameters at compile time.

title: Is-a or has-a?
statement: A Car needs an Engine. Which relationship is the better model?
options: Car inherits from Engine because they are related
Car has an Engine as a field (composition)
explanation: Inheritance models "is a" (a Car is not an Engine). A Car "has an" Engine, so the Car holds an Engine object. Composition is also easier to change later, for example swapping in an ElectricMotor.

title: Strings in JavaScript and Python
statement: In both JavaScript and Python, what happens when you try to change one character of an existing string in place?
options: It works and changes the string
Strings are immutable: you create a new string instead
explanation: Strings cannot be modified after creation. Operations like replace or slicing return new strings, and the original is unchanged.

title: Integer division
statement: In Python 3, what is the value of 7 // 2?
explanation: // is floor division and returns the largest whole number not exceeding 7 / 2 = 3.5, which is 3. The single slash gives 3.5.

title: Equality in JavaScript
statement: What does the expression  0 == "0"  evaluate to in JavaScript, and what about  0 === "0" ?
explanation: == converts operands to a common type before comparing, so the string "0" becomes the number 0 and the result is true. === compares without converting, and a number is not a string, so it is false. Prefer ===.

title: Mutating a list in a function
statement: A Python function receives a list and calls .append(4) on it. What does the caller see afterwards?
options: The original list now contains the 4
explanation: The parameter refers to the same list object as the caller's variable (the reference is passed by value). Mutating the object is visible to the caller; reassigning the parameter to a new list is not.

title: Breadth-first search
statement: Which data structure does breadth-first search use to decide which node to visit next?
explanation: BFS visits nodes in order of distance from the start, so nodes discovered first must be processed first. That is first-in first-out, a queue. Depth-first search uses a stack (or recursion).

title: Dynamic programming
statement: What property makes a problem a good fit for dynamic programming? (choose two)
options: The input must be a string
It must be solved with recursion only
The answer is always an integer
explanation: DP stores answers to subproblems that are needed repeatedly (overlapping subproblems), and builds the final answer from optimal answers to those smaller pieces (optimal substructure).

title: Joins
statement: Which SQL join returns all rows from the left table, with NULLs where the right table has no match?
explanation: A LEFT (OUTER) JOIN keeps every row of the left table. INNER JOIN keeps only matching pairs, and CROSS JOIN produces every combination.

title: HTTP status codes
statement: A client sends a request for a resource that does not exist. Which status code should the server normally return?
explanation: 404 means the resource was not found. 200 is success, 301 a permanent redirect, and 500 a server-side failure.

title: Version control
statement: What does git commit do?
options: Uploads your changes to the remote server
Records the staged changes as a new snapshot in your local history
explanation: A commit is local. It saves what you staged with git add. Sharing it with others needs git push.

title: Nested loops
statement: for i in 1..n { for j in 1..n { work() } }  runs work() how many times, and what is the complexity?
explanation: The inner loop runs n times for each of the n iterations of the outer loop, so work() runs n x n = n^2 times.
